key_insight: FOCUS shows that retinal AI models do not generalize uniformly: strong single-dataset performance often breaks under dataset shift, subgroup differences, and calibration checks.
clinical_relevance: For retinal screening tools, reliability across sites and patient groups matters as much as accuracy, making cross-dataset evaluation essential before clinical use.
method: Built a benchmark across 10 public fundus datasets spanning different geographies, acquisition settings, and label definitions.
Harmonized three tasks: binary diabetic retinopathy, referable diabetic retinopathy, and glaucomatous optic neuropathy.
Compared vision-only encoders, vision-language dual encoders, and multimodal LLMs using ranking, calibration, subgroup disparity, and image-quality robustness analyses.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 532 base model configurations plus 228 LoRA-adapted multimodal LLM configurations, showing mixed transfer across datasets rather than one universally best model family.
watch_item: Results from one dataset may not predict external performance, especially for calibration and subgroup fairness, so local validation is still necessary.
paper_title: FOCUS: Benchmarking Retinal Model Generalization from Foundation Vision Encoders to Multimodal LLMs
